utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Good morning, General. The affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, General Galevski.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you that we started discussing with the commissions yesterday as a method of work and you said that there was standing commissions that were envisioned with the rule-books and as well as ad hoc commissions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that these ad hoc commissions were linked to the discretionary estimate of the minister in reviewing certain issues and were not a legal obligation of the minister. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If -- and if someone were to claim that the establishment of the commission that you were a member of since August 13, 2001, was a disciplinary responsibility of the minister, that would also not be true. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, you said yesterday that depending on the issue that the -- the commission was established for, they would be lasting for a shorter or longer period. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that these commissions were actually with a certain purpose with the decision that they were established with, a task that was assigned by the minister to review or to decide upon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The standing commissions have -- had an established manner of work. They are rules of procedure and rule-book according to which they worked. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The ad hoc commissions were agreeing upon their method of work by themselves and actually that work and the method of work of those commissions was not envisioned in any rule-book. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. In principle, the basic rule that's applicable the ministry must be obeyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, I would like to ask you now to take the binder again, binder number 1 and to look at the document found in tab 37.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is P381, and we registered it as 65 ter 1D476, 1D4300, while the English version was 1D4302.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, the Prosecutor showed you this decision yesterday, a decision to establish the headquarters of the operative action Ramno dated 29th of May, 2001. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as far as I remember, you said that this operative action was established even earlier?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a similar decision made by the previous minister, Dimovska.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please turn to the document found in tab 38. That is 65 ter 1D477. The page is 1D4304. The English page is 1D4306. Do you see the document?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the left upper corner of the document you can see that this is a decision passed by the Ministry of Interior on 7th of March, 2001, and if you turn to the second page, that is 1D4305, and the English version is 1D4307, as you just said, this is a decision passed by the Minister Dosta Dimovska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the first page in item 4, again your name Risto Galevski is written in the capacity as the deputy and secretary of police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So as you explained to the question of my colleague the Prosecutor, these headquarters of commission of the operative action Ramno was established to organise, manage and coordinate certain measures and activities linked to this operative action, and if I were to suggest to you that that meant that you were supposed to gather information related to the condition of the crisis, about the attacks of the terrorist organisations that already started in January, that would actually be the basic task of this headquarters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to ask you about the methods of work of the operative action Ramno, would it be correct if I were to say that since -- since the start of this action all the bodies of the state and national security were obliged to send to the headquarters information that would relate to the behaviour of the NLA and the other terrorist groups in a summarized version or found through direct information through Official Notes or telegrams, if some event would happened in the field. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct that after that the expert staff that was serving the headquarters would make information to all of you that are listed here would provide information about some information that were important for this operative action and that information would then be sent to you as members of the headquarters of the operation action Ramno. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a headquarters of Ramno, you would later be informing the minister about the most important events. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say that all the information from the field were neither reaching nor it was possible to reach the minister but only the summary information speaking about the most important events, then this statement of mine would be true, because it would be impossible for the minister to receive all the information coming from the fields.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 40. Tab 40, that is 65 ter 1D479.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that, Your Honours, I would like to ask -- I would like seek to tender this document about the establishment of the headquarters of Ramno, 65 ter 1D477.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D112, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to see this document 65 ter 1D479 numbered in Macedonian 1D4312 and the English version is 1D4314. That is a decision of the Ministry of Interior dated 18th of June, 2001. General, it says here that minister Boskoski, on 18 June 2001, passed a decision to establish a commission to investigate the legitimacy of claims by ethnic Albanian residents of the Republic of Macedonia that members of the Ministry of the Interior were exceeding their authority? You can see that, right?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in item 1 we can see Major Zoran Jovanovski who at that time was your deputy. Isn't it correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the other version, in the English page 1D4315 -- it is 5, all right. This is my mistake. Basically the tasks are set forth as well as the reasons because of which the minister establishes this commission. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is one of the commissions that was of a standing character, a more permanent character, so to say?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the question of the Prosecutor you responded that the minister was -- had established the committee to investigate these cases and you said that this request to report all these violations committed by the police were also published publicly. Is this commission that was established by the minister and which was of a more permanent character?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can recall now that there was an announcement in the media that such a working group had been established and the committee whereby we called the citizens to report on all the potential violations by the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to come closer to the microphone, please, and to speak up a little bit for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So as one of the measures that was to prevent any abuse of the police or other authorised officials, the minister, after the first information that is happening within the Ministry of Interior had established such a commission in order to provide an opportunity to the citizens to openly report on any violation committed by the police. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And he did it very -- very soon after he became a minister in May 2001. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document in evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As Exhibit 1D113, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now, General, to look at the document found in tab 41. That is 65 ter 1D480, 1D4316, the English version is 4318. General, is it correct that on the 25th of June there were a spontaneous protest in Skopje in which parts of the police on the reserve forces participated as well as part of reserve forces of the army as well as a number of citizens from Skopje?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I remember that, because in my career I've never seen more people gathered at one place.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We can see this decision from 26th of June, so just one day later after these events whereby the minister establishes a commission to determine the reasons, the number of participants, the purpose, and the manner in which this public unrest was held at the night of 25th and 26 June, 2001. Would you agree with me that the minister immediately reacted at the situation that took place with these kind of a behaviour of the citizens?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he reacted immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the composition of the commission, Goran Mitevski, Jordan Arsovski and Zoran Dandarevski, could you agree with me that the minister considered that the most responsible persons in the ministry must take on this task and see why this protest of citizens happened?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the next page in item 3, this is 1D4317 and the English version is 1D4319. The commission was assigned a very short deadline to submit the preliminary information to the minister, meaning on the 29th of June, 2001. Would you agree with me that this would be the commission that had a specific task and was supposed to carry out that task in a rather short period of time?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that this deadline was quite short.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document as a Defence exhibit as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D114, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, General, now to look at the document in tab 42. That is 65 ter 1D483, 1D4328, and the English version is 1D4330. General, is it correct that already at the beginning of the crisis through various terrorist attacks there were a number of large crimes committed that is necessary to immediately investigate all these crimes regardless of the fact who committed them and who were the subjects of that perpetration?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look at this decision that was on 29th of May, 2001 passed to establish a Working Group and in Article 1, as we said, the task was set forth for this Working Group and it was decided to establish a Working Group to gather evidence for committed war crimes in the territory of the Republic of Macedonia, and we can see what was the composition of that commission of this group here. If you look at the exhibit in tab 43, which is 65 ter 1D482, 1D4324. That is a decision on amendments to the decision for establishment of the Working Group. We can see in the first Article that is related to this Working Group that we already saw before so it is the Working Group established on the 29th of May, 2001. That is visible in item 1. Do you see that document?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it is obvious from item 1 that this decision from 29 May 2001 number 16.1-16711/1 from 29th of May and 24th of June 2001 is again amended in certain provisions. Certain persons have been changed in the committee -- in the commission. May I ask you, sir, whether it would be correct that the Minister Boskoski was very often, due to dissatisfaction of the results of some of the members of the commission, was making amendments and giving incentives to the commission to work as successfully as possible. Is this your knowledge about the manner of the work of the minister in 2001?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is probably like that. Although I have never heard such a comment personally by the minister -- from the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But both these documents, the first and the second one, speak that the minister have been always thinking it is necessary to investigate all the individual cases of war crimes committed in the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask to tender these two exhibits 1D483 and 1D482 to be admitted as Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 1D483 will become Exhibit 1D115; and 65 ter 1D482 will become Exhibit 1D116, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, General, now to look at the documents in tab 44. That is 65 ter 1D485, and the number is 1D4334, and the English version is 1D4335. This is a decision dated 27th of January 2002, and you can see there by the composition of the -- of this Working Group. Could you tell us who Refet Elmazi is?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Refet Elmazi was at that time and is even now a deputy minister for the interior and he is an ethnic Albanian by his ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you can see, the task of this Working Group was to investigate some of the circumstances that took place already in May 2001 about the disappearance of certain members of the Albanian ethnicity. Is it correct, General, that this decision also confirms the fact that Minister Boskoski, during his tenure as minister, was attempting to not only through the normal lines of work that would -- that would be the basic obligations of the Ministry of Interior that is attempted by establishing certain Working Groups stimulate these bodies to conduct their duties as the best -- as good as possible and to contribute for a certain issue to be resolved. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, during the direct examination, the Prosecutor gave you some information about the events in Ljuboten. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you two decisions of the minister to establish committees to investigate certain circumstances of the Ljuboten events. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you for you to be shown Exhibit P73. This decision, as we saw earlier, was passed by the Minister Boskoski on the 13th of August, 2001. So immediately after the Ljuboten events. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you state the earlier, members of the committee were the most responsible persons, officers of the ministry at the time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And such selection made by the minister was justified because he believed that these could use his -- each of them could use his own line of command to make the entire MOI investigate this event into the most efficient and best possible way. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you saw earlier in any -- any decision establishing a committee would set forth the task, and in item 2, this committee was given the task that on the basis of data, reports and other available material of the services of the Ministry of Interior as well as on the basis of information learned from interviews with the members of the MOI would review the circumstances and analyse the activities under taken by the security organs. This was the task of the committee whose member you were. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to show the witness the document marked for identification --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the Prosecutor could help me, this is the decision establishing a committee of 7th of March, 2003. This is, I think, P379, MFI. I need the decision. The entire document is under this number, but I would like to see N000-8907, so the page that shows the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This decision was shown to you in the course of the examination-in-chief. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask to turn to the next page of this document, N000-8908. And in this item II, the minister, Hari Kostov, sets forth the task for this committee. He then ordered, this could be seen in the third line, the last three words in Macedonian, it to establish the composition and the capacity of the unit that took action in the aforementioned period, including the identification of each of the members of the unit individually to establish the reasons and responsibilities for the human casualties and the material damage in order to establish the truth about the aforementioned events, to investigate the use of legal powers of the unit as well as to identify the consequences of the action that was carried out. In the next paragraph it is stated that they need to take into account the findings and the reports from the forensic medicine institute, and in the next paragraph, they also have the task to establish the responsibility for the action that was carried out. Is my interpretation of the task given to this committee correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood -- I was reading what was written and it is not correct. This committee could not establish the responsibility. It could only raise the initiative to establish. It would be another committee that would actually establish the actual responsibility. Otherwise, everything else is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as we saw in the first page of this decision, this decision was passed on the 7th of March, 2003. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see it from the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it was passed after the exhumation and the post-mortem of the people in the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it was passed after the forensics medicine institute had the findings about the identity of the people killed, the way in which they were killed, and regarding other circumstances that could have been ascertained through the post-mortem. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, if I say that therefore the task of the committee and the circumstances and the possibilities for the committees were completely different?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they were completely different from one another.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before I continue with other questions, I would like to ask that the document we discussed with the witness a moment ago 65 ter 1D458 in tab 44 is also received as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D117, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, I would like to ask you now about something completely different, and actually it might already be clear, but I would like to repeat it. Is it correct that all persons of full age, once they serve conscription military service, have their reserve military deployment position?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that deployment position could be within the army of the Republic of Macedonia or in the police or in civilian protection. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All police reservists are essentially within the reserve forces of the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In a case of a state of war, state of emergency or when the security situation is under risk, then the reserve forces are called. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters have difficulties understanding what the witness says, so if he could speak up a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have been warned again. Could you please speak up more clearly. It was translated now, but I would like to ask you to speak more clearly in the future.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you stated when we were looking at the chart of the organisation chart of the Ministry of Interior and you testified there is defence preparation department within the ministry and at times of peace it also performs the planning and the training for the reserve forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There is also a general act establishing the way in which the reserve forces are called, and this part of the activities of the Ministry of Interior is also regulated by a rule-book?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 45. That is 65 ter 1D209, R042-4704 and the draft of the English translation is -- no, I apologise. So we have another number, 1D2311 that is the Macedonian, and the English is 1D2394. Do you see the text published in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia, that is the issue 9 of 1996. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The book of rules on the way of summoning and engaging members of the reserve forces of the Ministry of Interior, it was adopted by the then minister Ljubomir Frckovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the officers who are summoning the reserve forces have the duty at the moment when the head of the state makes a decision that the situation warrants summoning of the reserve forces and the minister then orders summoning of the reserve forces of the police, then the workers who work on the defence preparations do it in -- in -- according to this book of rules. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that in 2001, after the call for mobilisation, because the situation was insufficiently well understood by the citizens at the very beginning the response to the mobilisation was very poor, especially in the army?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that if it would be necessary to increase the number of the reserve forces in some municipality or in some region that is at higher risk of crisis, then the competent body for defence preparation of that municipality would need to request the Ministry of Defence of that branch -- in that municipality, to be allocated additional number of persons for the reserve forces of the police?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is exactly the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So am I right in saying that if the citizens of Macedonia of full age who have served their conscription military service, if they would be coming voluntarily to the police, although they were called volunteers, they were not volunteers. They were reserve military conscripts, only they would be in the ranks of other units; for instance the army. So if such persons would say come to the police station to volunteer then the police station would need to seek permission for them to be transferred from the reserve forces of the army into the reserve forces of the police. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. There were thousands of people who were standing in front of the police stations and asking to join the police, by normally not -- of course, not all of them have been accepted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me now, General, is it correct that for someone to become de facto and de jure member of the reserve forces of the police, they would first need to be in the list of the reserve forces of the police or transferred from the reserve forces of the army into the reserve forces of the police?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then they would need to be given a uniform and weapons?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from this, they would need to be registered in the list and receive the salary that was envisaged for the reserve forces. They would need to be issued an ID card for their membership in the reserve forces, and they would need to be assigned to certain tasks in the police station, or in any other body of the Ministry of the Interior. Only under those circumstances or conditions a person could be considered a police reservist. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if only one of these conditions is met, for instance, a uniform is issued, or if only weapons were received from some police station, or the fact alone that the people were involved in a combat or police action, that in itself would not mean that the person is a member of the reserve forces of the police and under your effective command and control. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The minister themself, regardless of whether it is the Minister Boskoski or the minister before him or the current minister, has nothing to do with establishing whether the persons should be in the reserve forces, who are the people who would be in the reserve forces and whether the conditions have been met for the persons joining the reserve forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 47. That is P85, 0424706, Macedonian, 65 ter number. R 042470 -- 406-ET is the English. This is the rule-book on the form and procedure to issue special ID for the members of the police force -- reserve forces of the Ministry of Interior. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it was passed in July, 2001. It could also be seen on this page. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that when you spoke a moment ago about this huge protest of people on the 25th of June, 2001 in which also part of the reserve forces of the police took part that then the minister, considering such conduct of the reserve forces, passed a decision on demobilisation but that already the next day the president of the state performing his duty as a commander of the Armed Forces requested that this decision is annulled. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was something of that sort, but I could not give you a precise nature or confirmation, although there were exchanges back and forth in the public, public pressures but I could not say with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In order to refresh your memory, I would like to ask you to look at the document in tab 48. That is 1D90, the Exhibit 1D90. 1D036 is the page, and the English is 1D4038. This is the summary overview by the Ministry of Interior, and in the middle here you see demobilisation of the reserve forces. And in the previous page you can see that it is the date 29th of June. It says here: "The minister of the interior Ljube Boskoski stated at a press conference the members of the reserve forces of the police of the Republic of Macedonia will be demobilised and withdrawn from the check-points around Skopje, in order to allow the politicians to continue the peaceful resolving of the problem." I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 49, in order to refresh your memory again. This is the Exhibit 1D91 page 1D4041, and the English page is 1D4042. It is stated here: "The police reserves are returning to the check-points. The Ministry of the Interior withdraws the decision demobilisation of the police reserve forces and ordered for remobilisation which will be processed selectively. The remobilisation of the police reserve forces is conducted upon a request of the commander in chief of the Macedonian Armed Forces, Boris Trajkovski, due to the current security situation in the country." Do you remember now, General, that this decision was issued and then withdrawn at the request of the president of the republic?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Exactly. I think this was the same reason, if I may be refreshed -- or if I may refresh my memory out loud, for the misunderstanding of the quarrel between the Minister Boskoski and the President Trajkovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask to go back to the Exhibit P85. That is in tab 47, and as we saw from this communication from the Ministry of Interior it is indicated that the reserve forces will be redeployed again but on a selective bases, considering that this rule-book established the duty that all reservists need to have their ID in that sense. Do you agree with me that this was also one of the measures that will make the distinction who is a member of the reserve police forces and who isn't?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I remember well. Its purpose was to overcome certain problems that existed before that in the reserve forces, so the idea was to completely improve the situation with regards to the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief the Prosecutor showed you some documents from the work of the other commission and among them was an Official Note by Miodrag Stojanovski, if I remember the name well, and your comment was that you learned about this for the first time when the investigator of this Tribunal questioned you. Do you remember having been shown something of the sort?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you then shown a list of some people who -- who were allegedly issued weapons in PSOLO?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, are you aware that Miodrag Stojanovski was an officer, the authorised officer in PSOLO, or are you not aware of this fact?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know my colleague Miodrag also personally and I know that he is administrator --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are not sure about the last part of the... Could the witness be asked to repeat the final part of the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... To get back on the police graduation parade ground and lift your voice more. You are speaking very quietly to yourself and the words are not coming across terribly well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was do you know Miodrag Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 51A. That is 65 ter 1D493.1, page 1D4455, and the English is 1D4456. This is a letter from the Ministry of Interior in response to the request of the Defence of Mr. Boskoski to obtain certain information related to the issuance of weapons from the police station PSOLO on the 25th and 26th of July. Considering that you were not shown the document about the persons who were issued weapons, I will not do it now, but I will tell you what was the response of the ministry to the request of the Defence. In paragraph 3 it is stated: "The persons whose names are in the tables represented by PSOLO were not police reservists. The persons were -- the aforementioned persons were not paid salary. The Ministry of Interior does not have any records that they had received training in Idrizovo, the persons whose names are written in the table were not issued police IDs." General, if those persons, regardless of their identity, were not meeting the conditions that were necessary for someone to become a reservist in the Ministry of Interior, would you also agree that they were not reservists in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to mark this document for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D118, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, I would like now to ask you to turn to another area which is certainly of interest to be analysed before this Court; at least this is the opinion of the Defence counsel. Could you please tell me if the structure of the police after the independence of the Republic of Macedonia, was this structure inherited from the previous structure of Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that even before it was dedicated special care, that all members of different nations and minorities are adequately represented within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, if we look at the percentage of individual minorities, then we would see this representation was not adequate to the given percentage of that minority in the Republic of Macedonia. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. You are reminding me of the time when I enrolled in the police school, if you allow me to explain, my generation of 120 cadets in the secondary police school. There were only seven to eight Albanians, two to three Turks, and I don't remember well the numbers. But then I came up -- when I was able, when I was in the position to get more information about this representation in police, I noticed that there was no such an interest at that time and it is after the conflict that this interest increased, the interest in the minorities to be more represented in these institutions increased.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You responded to part of my question. As you said, at the time there was no great interest on the part of the minorities. Do we speak of the Albanian population, can we say that they mainly live in the north western parts of Macedonia, in mountains, and they traditionally are -- that they traditionally are -- they traditionally have evolved in cattle breeding?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was a case, especially during the time when we were part a Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me, regardless of how difficult this would be for the members of that population, that these were people that at that time had the lower level of education and their tradition was not such as to send children to higher schools, such as the police school or army school and so on?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, is it also correct that the Republic of Macedonia, after its independence, has been aware of the fact that the minorities should be more involved in the state institutions, and as a result of that, has started to undertake measures to improve that situation?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that these efforts have continued to increase when after the elections in 1998 the coalition VMRO and two Albanian parties came into power?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not be very precise as far as 1998 is concerned, but I recall the year of 2000 when in the interior ministry a project evolved related to employing about 250 Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I will not make the next question because you responded already. I will ask you to look at the document in tab 53, 65 ter 1D465, page 1D47272, and English version 1D47274. This document is also a document from the interior ministry from the international affairs and European integration division. You can see that this is a report, and this is negotiations regarding training for newly recruited police officers in cooperation with the US embassy in the Republic of Macedonia. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this report for the first time, though I knew this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 1 we can see that this meeting was held in order to discuss the assistance and training of 500 newly recruited police officers and the fifth line in Macedonian, we can see that the meeting was attended by Colonel Galevski. Is this you?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was -- this is me, but since here, I don't recall that I participated to this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is why we have sometimes written documents that can remind us. Thank you. Now, please look at paragraph 2 of this document which says: "The training programme is aimed at increasing the number of police officers from ethnic minorities living in the Republic of Macedonia and priority will be given to ethnic Albanian applicants. This programme is to be completed by October 2002. The training will be performed successively in groups of approximately 100 candidates." Further on in line 1, the two last lines it says that the exact number of -- of 100 candidates to be recruited in the first phase in addition to public campaign of public information. On page 1D4273 and 75, the English version, in the fourth indent, it says that the training should start on July 1st, 2001, and should last for 12 weeks, after which the newly trained police officers will need to be deployed on the ground. Does this report now remind you of the works you have been doing at the beginning of 2001, together with the American minister of justice?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: How wouldn't I recall, since I was the one to implement this in the beginning of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that before you have ever started with the implementation of this program you have in fact started to implement it by introducing mixed police patrols in mixed areas where Albanians -- where there were Albanian population.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did this as much as we could and where we could do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, is it correct that the attacks of extreme Albanian groups in fact slowed down this procedure that you had established with this programme?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only they slowed down the implementation, I think they managed to interrupt this -- the implementation because a lot of Albanian police officers probably frightened finding themselves in an uncertain situation stopped coming to work. Some -- only a few of them came at work but they didn't want to go to field works and some of them joined gangs in the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, General, that Ljube Boskoski, together with a deputy minister, Albanian Refet Elmazi on March the 8th went to a border village called Brest where here -- where such a police patrol office was supposed to be established as a pilot one to bring to this population humanitarian aid because it was attacked by these terrorist groups and then at that occasion a policeman was killed?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember very well this event but I don't recall the date, exactly whether it was the 8th. I know it was Spring 2001 and that at that time I was still deputy to the under-secretary for police. The initial plan was for me to head the police unit that would go there with humanitarian aid, with clothes and food, and to establish in the village of Gosince a temporary police station to keep order and peace in the village of Gosince and the nearby villages due to the problems of the Albanian population had from these terrorist groups, but then the plan changed. My superior at the time Mr. Domcev [phoen] came and said that he would go, because the police convoy would be also joined by Refet Elmazi and the state secretary Ljube Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this was the way in which these terrorist groups prevented or from establishing order and peace and from involving more Albanians in the police?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, and I would add that I remember when about 30 -- that -- I remember that we included about 30 Albanians that went to Gosince and to Brest at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, is it correct, General, that immediately after the signature of framework agreement you continued to implement the programme that you had established before?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask to you look at the document in tab 54. This is 65 ter 1D4666, 1D427, the English 1D4277. In this announcement, in the Vecer newspaper from September 3rd, 2001, in the left upper corner we see that the Ministry of Interior is issuing a public announcement for recruitment of 100 trainee police officers for an undefined work period. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This public announcement also says that the commission for the recruitment will be established. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This announcement was published also in Albanian newspapers and in newspapers in Turkish languages. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the document in tab 55, 65 ter 1D467, 1D4279 we can see here that the -- the announcement in one of the two languages. This one is in Albanian language. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So in tab 55 --

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I was waiting for your reply because only your reply enters the transcript, not your nodding. Could you please look at 56 now. It's 1D468, and 4281 and the Macedonian -- and the English, I'm sorry, is 4282. And can you see here the same announcement published in Turkish language, because there is also a Turkish minority in Macedonia. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you also look at the document in tab 57, you will see -- this is 65 ter 1D469, 1D4283, and 4284. You can see that the assistant minister sends this note and informs the police stations that an announcement was published for their recruitment of 100 new police officers. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to you look at a document tab 68. This is 65 ter 1D470, 1D4285 is the Macedonian version, and 1D4286 is the English version. In this document, can you see that on September 13, while this announcement was -- was published, a commission was established for the admission of trainee police officers in the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct that upon this announcement not 100 but 107 trainee police officers from -- proceeding from the minorities, most of them Albanians, were employed in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 107 and 109, I may be mistaken. One or two of them very soon, they left the training. They didn't pass a test, I think. Not -- they were not mostly Albanian; all of them were Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that after this the training continued of the remaining number of those foreseen by the programme within the academy where you became a director later. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. This process that was established continued until its full completion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, if I say that the -- the ethnic representation or the unequal representation of minorities in the state institutions including the interior ministry were not a reason for terrorist groups to start attacks in the Republic of Macedonia since these minority groups had their rights guaranteed and they were already participating to ongoing programmes with the view of improving the position of minorities in the country?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, now I would like to tender into exhibit one by one the documents that I have shown to the documents [as interpreted] So far. This is first 65 ter 1D465, the report on the programme by the ministry of justice and the American embassy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D119, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then 65 ter 1D466. This is the public announcement for the employment of 100 trainee police officers published in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D120, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then document 65 ter 1D467. This is the announcement in Albanian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D121, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then document 65 ter 1D468, the announcement in Turkish language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D122, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then 65 ter 1D469, the letter of assistant minister to all the police station sectors for the employment of new police officers in the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D123, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, finally, 65 ter 1D470, decision to form a commission for admission of trainee police officers in the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D124, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Having got through that lot, Ms. Residovic, I wonder whether this would be a natural moment to break.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We will go to the other binder of documents. We have just completed this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have been promoted to grade 2. Very well. We will adjourn now and we will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, we have partly already talked about the situation as it was in 2001 in Macedonia. You have testified also about certain terrorist attacks and my question is whether it is correct that these attacks had started already in January 2001.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. On 21st January, I think, this was the first attack against the police station in Tearce.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And after that terrorist attack other terrorist attacks followed at other places as well. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Most of the attacks or the most endangered areas were the area of Tetovo, Kumanovo and Skopje. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The sabotage terrorist groups attacked police stations and police patrols, military facilities, journalist teams, workers going to work and civilian population. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And along these attacks, large part of Macedonian population that lived in mixed areas were compelled to leave their homes.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said before something about the Albanians in the police. Is it correct that these groups used forceful methods against the Albanian citizens demanding from them to -- for these civilian to offer them support, and if they didn't, they were threatened?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had such information that, in addition to terrorising the non-Albanian population, the Albanian population was also terrorised. They wanted at least one person of their familiar to be recruited in the NLA and if they refused they were required to give a certain amount of money. I wouldn't like to speculate. It was about five to six Deutschemarks or five to 7.000 Swiss francs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said a while ago, and I want to make now a general question, is it correct that the members of this terrorist groups which later on were named members of the NLA had a very cruel behaviour towards the Albanians that were employed in Macedonian services or authorities in the areas where they -- they were?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. There were some examples, I remember one such example. They went once in the house of one of our colleagues, police officer, he was required to be recruited. He refused and for a while he was compelled to hide in the Tetovo police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You might be aware that when Ljube Boskoski and the deputy minister, Refet Elmazi were attacked during their visit to Brest in March 2001, their Albanian hosts, after this event, were also exposed to some revengeful actions?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not directly informed about that, but later on I got such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Ministry of Interior you had information that these terrorist groups very often crossed the border with Kosovo and they were also connected to the terrorist groups that conducted certain terrorist activities in the south of Serbia around Podujevo and Presevo?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Podujevo. Yes, that's correct. In fact, they are the ones that started the whole thing in Macedonia. They were only later joined by people from Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say now, General, that in those attacks the NLA used methods typical for other terrorist organisations, such as kidnapping, helding hostage of civilians, both Macedonians and Albanians, kidnapping and holding as hostages members of the Macedonian security forces, the army and the police, and among them also members of the Albanian ethnicity who were treated as traitors then that they physically ill-treated and intimidated civilians, for instance, workers of Mavrovo [phoen] company, then that they blackmailed and used other ways of intimidating the population, that they were seizing and destroying the property of Macedonians but also of a part of the Albanian population as well, that with this intimidation they caused the population to move out, displacement of population, that by force they restricted the right to movement, that they mined and blocked roads, that they were organising ambushes, that they would change into civilian clothes during the time they were not actively involved in any action or immediately after the action, would this summary that I've made of the modes and methods of activity of the NLA, would correspond to what you have witnessed in 2001?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. If you wish, I could give you a more precise specific cases, but mainly what you stated is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that towards the middle of 2001 the NLA started presenting data about its alleged organisation and in that significantly increasing its -- or presenting as greater their numbers and power, speaking about brigades, headquarters, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe this was their tactics of conduct in the field, and in that way, they would provide an incentive for the members of the Albanian ethnicity in Macedonia to join them, speaking about brigades, et cetera, 112th, 116th Brigade, I don't know what else, to make it seem that they are very powerful, very strong in numbers, very well equipped and that -- that they will reach the goal that they have set for themselves and that was seizing and then separating or cessation of a greater part of the territory of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct, General, that the Macedonian police often in agreement with the representatives of the international community withdrew from certain police stations in order to avoid casualties, especially casualties in the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. There are numerous such examples, numerous villages where this was -- this strategy was employed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So in this rough summary of the situation would it be correct that the Macedonian public and the Macedonian population was not only surprised by also shocked and placed in a very difficult situation, because they did not expect this?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that the information were fully clear, and this is why the public in Macedonia was so surprised and concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, it would be difficult for anyone to expect that the crisis from Kosovo would spill over to Macedonia, because Macedonia has hosted, during the NATO attacks about 300.000 Albanians from Kosovo, although it is a poor country and it could not provide a lot for its own citizens. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult for me to speak on this topic. It is not only correct, it is it more than correct, because in 1999 I was -- after, I was one of the heads in the police in the Ministry of Interior. We were literally placed in the role of the service for the refugees from Kosovo, and this is why it was very difficult for us when we experienced such a feedback from that situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you certainly, because you were head of certain services in the Ministry of the Interior, know that Ljube Boskoski, during that time, was one of the coordinators who worked on the admission and security for the refugees from Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know he held another job then before he was appointed a minister in this bodies, committees, governmental committee, I don't remember the exact office that he held at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to this, is it correct that after the events of Kosovo and the return of the Albanian population, the international community gave a huge recognition to the Republic of Macedonia on several occasions for the assistance that it offered then to both the Albanian population and the forces of the international community?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that when the first casualties were caused by these terrorist attacks gradually Macedonian population started protesting, which made the public law and order situation in the country even more complex?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct, and it happened very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And among first such big protests was the protest of tens of thousands of people in Bitola in May and June 2001?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I was personally present in Bitola during the first one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The police and you and the ministry supporting your forces in the field undertook all measures to firstly prevent such situation and then if the situation happens, to then undertake measures for the -- to avoid repetition of such situation?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in relation to these, let me call them unfortunate events in Bitola the SVR Bitola and the police organs have detained several dozens of people who were violating public law and order and there were also criminal reports or charges filed in relation to about 100 persons to the competent Prosecutor's office. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you stated at the beginning of this cross-examination that you were enforcing the laws of the Republic of Macedonia, the criminal charges were on the basis of crimes provided in the criminal code of the Republic of Macedonia or the law on misdemeanours of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look into the second binder. Have you taken it? Because we have finished with the first one.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document in tab 59 --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we would like to request marking of this document for identification after it is shown to the witness and later, according to the Rule 92 bis we will also submit to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You here the statement of Kristo Zdravkovski. Do you know who Kristo Zdravkovski is?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement it is read: "I Kristo Zdravkovski, current head of SVR Bitola, was head of SVR Bitola also in course of 2001, when, during mass demonstrations in Bitola, public law and order was disturbed to a greater extent. When many business and residence facilitates in the city were arsoned and damaged. According to my recollection, the events took place at the beginning of the month of May, and the month of June in 2001, and took place for the duration of two days each. In relation to these events SVR Bitola undertook appropriate operative measures and activities as a result of which there was not a single human casualty in the events, while there were some 2.000 or 3 citizens who took part of them. Furthermore, in the course of the operative work, the SVR Bitola identified the perpetrators of criminal offences pursuant to Article 292, in relation to the Article 288 of the criminal code of the Republic of Macedonia as well as pursuant to Article 385 of the criminal code of the Republic of Macedonia. As I remember, many criminal reports were filed against about 100 perpetrators for the stated criminal offences and those criminal reports were processed by the public prosecutor's office in Bitola. As I remember, the public prosecutor's office further processed the criminal reports to the Basic Court in Bitola; however, after the amnesty law entered into force in the Republic of Macedonia, the criminal procedures were terminated. Is this statement of Kristo Zdravkovski something that corresponds to your knowledge about 2001 about the way in which the police reacted to the disturbances of public law and order?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fully agree with this text. I would also add that the police was in a really dire situation, I would say to re-establish public law and order because it needed a wall, more composed of humans or tampon zones in order to protect the properties and the lives of several citizens of Bitola who were targeted by the protesters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have this document marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D125, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now, General, to look at the document in tab 60, this is 65 ter 428, and let's look immediately at the page N005-1053, and the English, 1053-ET. This is -- it is still not on the screen. And I would like N005-1503 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure about the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Earlier we discussed it and you answered several questions related to the events of the 25th of June, 2001. This is the analytics department of the Ministry of Interior for the city of Skopje which has written the information about the events on 26th of June. In the last paragraph of this information, in the second sentence the following is mentioned: "At 2340, the General Risto Galevski addressed the present and called reservists to return to the places where they were deployed and then he told the citizens that those who are deployed as police reservists should go" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Who had the status of police reservists, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- "should go to the corresponding police stations and be activated." Is this an information, General, which speaks about the event that you testified about earlier where also the reserve forces of the police participated as well as the reserve forces of the army of the Republic of Macedonia with a large number of citizens?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 61. This is 65 ter 1D481. It is 1D4320, and the English is 1D4322. And you see that this is an information coming from the Ministry of Interior about the events which took place on the 25th of June, 2001, in front of the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia. And I would like to ask you to look together at paragraph 3. It says: "During the aforementioned period of time, over a very brief period as a result of a spontaneous reaction, the people gathered in front of the parliament were joined by the citizens of the city of Skopje which had as a consequence an enormous increase in the number of persons present, around 3.000 or 4.000 people. In the meantime the mass was joined by a smaller group of active members of the police forces as well as a group of members of the army of the Republic of Macedonia." Is this what took place on that day, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only I don't agree with this information. I haven't seen it then with the number of people. I believe it was far greater than three or 4.000 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And on the second page of this document, 1D4321, in the fourth paragraph, again it is mentioned that at 2340 you addressed this mass of people, and you tried to calm down the situation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that at that moment there was a huge dilemma present whether to use force against this protesters but that it was decided and it was decided by the assistant for Skopje Etremov, the director for the security of the public security bureau, that it could not be done, because many of the protesters were armed and this would lead to bloodshed. And this is why you personally tried to calm these mass of people down. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And we saw a while ago the minister established immediately the next day a group that was to investigate whether there were organisers to this gathering, and if you recall, the final conclusion was that those were spontaneous protests because of the way in which the members of the NLA left Aracinovo at the moment when the army and the police would have been able to completely free Aracinovo?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I understood the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we will start again. Is it correct that on the 22nd of June, in a joint action of the army and the police, Aracinovo was virtually freed, but then NLA requested cease-fire and upon a request of the NATO representatives, they asked that they are left -- to leave the village. The authorities of the Republic of Macedonia accepted this. They provided buses, but the NLA left the village armed, and that was the immediate cause for these protests. Have I refreshed your recollection, or do you think that there were any other reasons that I failed to investigate yet?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understood you now completely. This is correct. The public was greatly disturbed when they heard that the police and the army were withdrawing from Aracinovo and rumours were spread that the state authorities, the high state authorities were actually traitors of the Republic of Macedonia, that this was a treason, probably they were not aware of the plans of the leadership and the activities under way at that moment. Otherwise, the order to withdraw from Aracinovo, I received from the Minister Ljube Boskoski personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that on the 5th or 6th of June, somewhere around that time, upon a proposal of the government of the Republic of Macedonia, cease-fire was signed between the representative of the army and the police, on the one hand, the Armed Forces of the Republic of Macedonia and the representative of NATO who was supposed at that moment to guarantee the cease-fire on behalf of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct. On the 5th of July, or the 4th, in the evening, I received an order from the minister via the telephone to go to the headquarters of the army of Republic of Macedonia that a statement needed to be signed in relation to cease-fire, termination of the activities in the field. And together with the head of the General Staff, Pande Petrevski, we signed that statement. I think it was addressed to the NATO representative at that time in Macedonia, Mr. Peter Faith, and some other ambassador, I don't remember the name at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me, General, that this decision of the government of the Republic of Macedonia and the president of the Republic of Macedonia who had previously tabled a long-term plan for a peaceful resolution of crisis was a decision of strategic importance that obligated the Ministry of the Interior to act accordingly?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And could you say, because you were one of the signatories to this agreement, that actually you did not accept, not then and not ever, accept the NLA as the other party, and you never negotiated with them anything and you never signed with them anything?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct, General, that even after that signing of the agreement and the guarantee by NATO on behalf of the NLA, the NLA continued to violate the cease-fire and there were numerous consequences actually exactly during the period of cease-fire. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is more than correct. Because the greatest losses and damage were caused actually after the signing of that statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask to you look at the document in tab 64. This is 65 ter 398, and it is dated 25th of July, 2001. That is page N004-9892, Macedonian, while the English page is the same, only ET.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter will repeat the number because I was not sure about it, 9812.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, this is an information from the SVR Skopje again, so sector Skopje, department for analytics, and its subject is the security situation in the city and why the region in the period from 1800 to 2400 hours on 25th of July, 2001. My question is, General, is it correct that the protest of citizens of Macedonia were increasingly taking place in the city of Skopje, which created enormous difficulties in maintaining the public law and order in the city?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct. Almost constantly there would be a smaller or a greater group that protested in front of the parliament, in front of the government on a square or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 25th of June but also in the protests later, the police of Skopje tried to protect the parts of the city where the Albanian population lived, so that these protests are not targeting that population?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember precisely. On that evening, there were rumours in front of the parliament that someone is trying to incite the Macedonian population and make them cross the bridge towards the other side of the river Varda, but in consultations with the head of the General Staff of the Republic of Macedonia we undertook specific police measures and activities.
