We organised cordons, human shields of police officers on the bridges and we prevented the crowd from transferring to the other side, and they were prevented in those intentions that were manifested.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you now to look at the document in tab 65. This is 65 ter 1D475, page 1D4295, Macedonian, and the English is 1D4298. That is also an information from the sector for police Skopje, analytics department, and subject of this information as well, as you can see, is protest of the citizens from the Tetovo villages where the citizens of Skopje also joined several cars of civilians and of OSCE were damaged around the city. Page 1D4296 and page 1D4299 of the English version, we can see that the police have taken an inventory in the city of Skopje of all the facilities that were damaged as private property by the protesters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we look at the document that is in the tab 66, that is 65 ter 405, that is N004-9837, and the English version is the same number with the addition of the ET. This document also speaks about protests that have taken place on the 8th of August this time in Skopje. And those were the protests of the Tetovo residents as well as numerous citizens of the capital as well, whereby also some facilities of the citizens have been damaged. Mostly these were ethnic Albanian residents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The protesters were Macedonians.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the damaged facilities?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't confirm, but their purpose was to damage the facilities of the Albanians, but somehow they managed to damage some facilities that belonged not only to the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that the police of the city of Skopje did their best and have brought in a large number of persons who participated in the damaging of the citizens' property and misdemeanour and other measures have been taken against many of them as well as the looted property was also seized from them, the property that was looted from the damaged facilities.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true that the police did their best to carry out the function, the task that was assigned to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like ask to you look at document in tab 67. It is 65 ter 1D440. The page is 1D4043 in the Macedonian version and 1D4046 of the English version. Again, this is a document from the sector of the interior of Skopje, dated 9th of August, 2001, and the subject is individuals who violated the public law and order and committed robberies on 8th of August, 2001. General, is this information -- does this information contain information about the measures that the Skopje police have taken after the protests that we spoke about that was information contained in the previous documents?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 1 it is visible that in the Centar and Bit Pazar police station that a total of 44 persons have been brought in, and at this as well as at the other pages, 1D404 and 1D405 in the Macedonian version, and English page is 1D4047 and 4048. We can see that all the persons that were brought there are listed and against whom some measures have been taken. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask now, since this last document that I showed, 65 ter 440, since it has not been admitted in evidence, to be tendered as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would also seek to tender the document 65 ter 605 as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Counsel may be referring to 405, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 405. I apologise, I was reading fast, so, Your Honours, as far as I understood, you said that the first 65 ter 1D440 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 126, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I now seek to tender as a Defence exhibit document number 65 ter 405. That is the information about the protests of the Tetovo residents in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 1D127, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would also seek to tender as Defence exhibit, document 65 ter 475 of 25th of July. That is the information about the protests of the Tetovo village residents protests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D128, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also seek to tender as Defence exhibit 65 ter 398 which is the information about the security situation in the city and the vicinity of the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D129, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also seek to tender as Defence exhibit document 65 ter 1D481, speaking about the information on the events on the 25th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D130, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General -- I apologise. I was warned that there's one more document to be tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is document in tab 61. Document 61 has already been admitted, but 65 ter 428 has not been admitted. That is a second information about the events in front of the Macedonian parliament of 26th of June, 2001, coming from the security sector of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D131, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, in this time of a situation which was difficult -- in which it was difficult to maintain the public law and order in the capital and in the other areas, would it be true that -- that in the course of the action to conquer the terrorist and diversion groups already in March the army of the Republic of Macedonia joined as well?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they joined.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that during the first months the president of the country as a supreme commander of the Armed Forces or -- issued orders only to the army troops but given the complicated situation starting from May, he started using his authority to ask and to issue orders to the police forces as well?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think there was misunderstandings about the competencies, the rights and the -- and the authority, but the rights that are given to the president of the country with the session of the Security Council, I think that they found some legal basis to put the police to a grand extent under his command as part of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When saying that, would my statement be correct that these misunderstandings were because of the fact that the parliament did not proclaim a state of war? In the given situation, it was necessary to establish a single command and control so the president used his authority deriving from the law on defence and was asking to put the police forces under his command, was that the way in which this dispute was resolved?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So when your police forces, regardless whether those were the Tigers or the posebna unit, when they participated in the fights against Tetovo, Vaksince and other areas, then basically they were acting upon the single command of the army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Practically I couldn't say it was so, but together with the military command we used to sit together and to work jointly. Also, the question remained open who is superior to whom or who commands to whom.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In mid year, in June, the Law on Defence was changed and then the authority to use the police units in the combat activities was transferred from the president of the country to the government of the Republic of Macedonia, but that required to adopt certain by-laws. Is it correct that up until those by-laws were adopted, the president still behaved and carried out his authority as a supreme commander of the Armed Forces?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that was the law that was amended or a new law was adopted, I can't remember, but it never became operational with that kind of competence between the government and the president regarding the police and the army, because that law required the adoption of certain by-laws that would be the tool for its implementation which were not adopted, so the old law remained in force. That is to say, it was -- that was the law that was applied.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, since you at that time headed the police forces, that -- it was neither the old nor the new law who gave authority to the minister to ask for the use of the police force in the combat activities?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I -- I'm just trying to make sure that the record is clear. The witness in his response to the last question said that the old law remained there in force, and I don't then understand why my colleague is saying, well, is it correct that neither the old nor the new law gave authority to the minister. It seems that the witness has answered the question. The old law is in force. Unless I'm not understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There seems to be some uncertainty, Ms. Residovic. The witness may be able to clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you might look at the document in tab 72. That is Exhibit 1D98, and this is the Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia of June 1, 2001, where the new Law on Defence was published. Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the final provisions of this law, found at page R 042-4559, it is Article 172. The English text would be on page -- it's 002850. And these final provisions, transitional and final provisions, it is stipulated that regulations issuance of which is foreseen by this law will be issued in a period of one year from the day it is put in effect except for the regulations foreseen in the Articles 142, 143, and 144, chapter 12, planning which will be passed in two years at the most. The following Article, number 173, reads: "With the day of this law getting into effect, the -- the law on defence ceases to be in force," and we can see the number 30/95. The next paragraph also says, "Supplemental regulations issued in accordance with the law from paragraph 1 will be applied until the adoption of the provisions of Article 172 of this law if they are not in collision with the provisions of this law." So, General, my question is, and I also understood that your answer also was that since the -- these regulations were not passed that were to regulate also the issues in the heading of the police forces practically in 2001 in respect to this competences, the old law was in force, which gave that authority to the president of the republic. Did I understand well what you just said previously?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since the new law as we can see in this text, since it has been published and was in effect on 1st of June, 2001, my next question, which caused certain uncertainty was the following. Is it correct that also this law from 1995 nor the law from 2001 did not foresee that the minister is the one who is authorised to order the use of the police forces in military or combat activities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, in -- while performing all your duties in the defence and the maintenance of law and order, is it correct that from the very beginning you had the closest cooperation with the international community?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was completely normal, it was also necessary at those moments.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that execution of the joint tasks is it true that the international community from the very beginning had a clear position about the situation in Macedonia and that the representative of the biggest world forces in the United States of America as well as Russia and other countries, then the Security Council and their representatives of the NATO completely supported the efforts made by the Republic of Macedonia and the attacks of these groups were either called extremist groups or were called terrorist groups. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. All until sometime 22nd of June, as far as I can remember and note, when this picture suddenly changed and created a dilemma and I still have a dilemma why this picture changed since -- I'm not sure whether that was exactly 22nd or 23rd of June, after the cease-fire order for Aracinovo came by the minister, that these three or -- two or three days before the great protest in front of the parliament I got a task from the minister together with a NATO vehicle, I think it was medical vehicle of NATO, to go towards Aracinovo and to withdraw some person that was wounded. I don't pose this dilemma by accident here. Maybe it's not part -- shouldn't be part of my testimony, but I think it is very important in my opinion who -- this is a question that deserve -- this deserve an attention by me, by the minister to withdraw this person from the village and to take it to the medical facilities, I never learned of his face or his identity, to have this person boarded on a helicopter and transferred to a hospital in the Bonstil base in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you provided quite a wider question -- quite a wider answer to the question that I posed, because I didn't know those facts. But my question would be, would it be correct that sometime in June the international community, at least its representatives that you contacted with, suddenly and without any reasons that they would communicate to the Macedonian authorities started to change the position towards these extremist and terrorist groups?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I already mentioned it. If I would learn what was the identity of the person that we saved from Aracinovo, I think that at least to me, many of the dilemmas would become more clear and I'm sure that also some other people's dilemmas would be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that part of these rallies of citizens that we spoke about were also due to the confusion that reigned among the population whether Macedonia was betrayed by the international community at that point?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, such confusion was created even amongst some of our colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, despite that fact, you continued to give utmost support and cooperation to all the international organisations, NATO, OSCE, and others in the country. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Moreover, you were aware that without the assistance of the international community. You were unable to do some of the things on your own.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the Ministry of Interior gave all possible open opportunities to the international community to access all areas under the control of the police of the Republic of Macedonia, and the police removed any obstacle that would be found on the ground to allow the international community to conduct its work?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. They had this big cards on their chest that left them free access and free -- and they were free to conduct all their activities in that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it was not the case only to -- as far as the international organisations were concerned, the police gave free access also to journalist teams and other NGOs to freely control the activities of the police and the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is exact. This can be verified as far as every discussion that was conducted by our side with the journalists.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that respect, very often you received both written and verbal recognitions from the international community?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask to you look at the document in tab 87. This is it Exhibit 1D38, page 1D1919 and the English version is 1D1920. You can see here a letter from the OSCE addressed to the Minister Ljube Boskoski signed by the deputy head of the OSCE mission Mr. Robin Seford. Have you met Mr. Seford?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken I think he was deputy head of the OSCE mission in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you can see here the letter that the minister received, and the deputy head of the mission thanks the minister for all the efforts and activities that the interior ministry has conducted in view of allowing for the OSCE to conduct its mission. Is this the content of the letter you see before you at the moment?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you were at a high-ranking position at that time and you can personally testify, could you say that this was a true behaviour, not only a diplomatic vocabulary addressed to the minister, namely was this a real gratitude that was felt in regards to the efforts invested by the police?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if someone would say that this was only a kind of diplomatic nice gesture, then this would not be accurate?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't. I would add not only the OSCE but other representatives of the international organisations shared the same opinion. At least this is what they said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like ask you, General, to tell me, while we already spoke of Aracinovo and your effort to allow [indiscernible] from Aracinovo, is it correct that whenever it was necessary to establish the facts on-site concerning alleged crimes that there would be an investigation team composed of investigating judge, prosecutor, and a group that would be established by that judge, composed of forensics and all those people, that were supposed to go to make the on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you have enumerated all the actors that are supposed to participate in such an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We speak of Aracinovo, since there have been considerable fights and the victims on both sides, is it correct that an investigating group with a judge, a prosecutor and representatives of the police who were not able to enter the village with the active involvement of the international community, this is the reason why representatives of the OSCE and the NATO accompanied them?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me clarify this. The previous days where there were victims among -- on our side and on the other side as well, it was impossible to make an on-site investigation. The investigation was done after the terrorists raised their white flags on the windows when the cease-fire was occurred after their retrieval together with international community with the representatives of the OSCE, the monitoring mission, the NATO, and our own team together with the prosecutor, with investigating judge and with forensic team, we entered and we made this on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could we turn now to the document in tab 62, 65 ter 400 N004-1819, Macedonian version. The English version, it's 9820-ET. So in tab 62 --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page in the English version, please. It's 9820. Macedonian version should stay the same. Please get back the Macedonian page as it was. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you see, General, this is an information on the current situation on the territory of the village of Aracinovo, and the measures and activities undertaken by the Ministry of Interior Affairs. It refers exactly to the event that you testified about a few moments ago. In paragraph 2 of this information, it says: "In this respect, after meetings held with representatives of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, the OSCE, the EU and NATO on June 27 at around 9.00 in the village of Aracinovo five police teams entered. Each of the teams comprised ten policemen from the unit posebna, one policeman each of Albanian ethnicity as well as authorised officials of the sectors for anti-terrorism and crime technique who were accompanied by public prosecutor, investigating judge, and representatives of the international monitoring mission." Under the -- headed by senior police officers the terms carried out an inspection and search of the terrain when several trenches were discovered as well as machine-gun and sniper nests, a large quantity of weapons and explosive devices were found mainly of Chinese production." Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the second page of this document, the following page, N004-9820, Macedonian version, and the English version is 9821-ET, and the third paragraph in the Macedonian version says: "After successful action of cleaning the area of the village Aracinovo which was also confirmed by international organisations the Ministry of Internal Affairs undertook activities to protect the property and personal security of the local inhabitants." Further on, on the same page, the fourth paragraph says: "Otherwise, during the planning and the execution of these activities, the ministry continued its cooperation with the representatives of the international monitoring mission in order to exchange experience and in view of establishing a more efficient way of carrying out the activities of the police staff on this territory." General, does this information remind you of the successful cooperation with the international community whose assistance helped you to make an on-site investigation in Aracinovo and to undertake all other necessary measures in order to restore peace and order and protect the civilian inhabitants there ?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tendered this information into an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D132, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that during this cooperation that you tried to continue and develop, you were also reviewing issues of cease-fire, then border crossing of groups, you were trying to convey all your information to the KFOR and requested that KFOR would also participate in the stabilisation of the situation in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not be very precise in responding. I cannot even enumerate all the people we had to discuss and to speak with. We had an endless number of contacts and with different people and organisations and among them there was KFOR as well. I was at one meeting in the Gazela factory, the shoe factory Gazela where there was such a meeting with the KFOR.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But as you said before, in -- by the end of June or by the end of the summer you could already feel that this cooperation with international community was more and more featured by a certain pressure excerpted upon the government the Republic of Macedonia and the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I don't know whether there was a written record of the meeting that was held in the Bellevue Hotel in those days. If there is such a document and such record I think that we could see there certain aspects concerning the plan for the retrieval of the NLA from the Aracinovo village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at the document in tab 89 of the binder. This is 65 ter 459 N005-1626, the English version, 1626-ET. This is an information related to a meeting with KFOR representatives in July 19th, 2001. Paragraph 1 -- in this paragraph we can see that the meeting was held on July 18th, 2001, and that this meeting was also attended by the assistant head of the department for police, Zoran Jovanovski. Was this your deputy at the time?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zoran Jovanovski was my deputy at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this meeting one additional attempt by the minister of the interior, in cooperation with NATO and KFOR, to ensure the execution of the previously prepared plan for the disarmament of these extremist terrorist groups? This plan had foreseen earlier for that weapon to be handed over in the period of 30 days.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was one of those activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D133, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, I would like to ask you now to go to this third binder. Before that, could you please answer to some questions related to your activities in August 12th, 2001. We will not go into the documents yet, but if we are to show some of them they will be in this third binder. First I would like to make you some questions. Earlier you said that on the 11th, together with the police forces you were in Radusa which had been attacked by these terrorist or NLA groups. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was there together with the active police was deployed there with the posebna unit and with the Special Unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With the posebna unit and the Special Unit Tigers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that before that, major attacks occurred from the NLA against army and police positions and your assessment was that this -- the purpose of these attacks was to prevent the signature of the framework agreement. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, these major attacks of the NLA included the first the attack of the army convoy in Karpala [phoen] where ten soldiers were killed and which resulted with the resignation of the Chief of Staff and the attack on the Ljubotenski Bacila where eight soldiers of the army were killed and a lot of them were wounded, then this was followed by the attack against the Radusa police station on the 8th and 10th of August. Are those the events that have occurred in that -- following that dynamic and having such serious repercussions?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that after that on 11th, late in the evening after you returned from Radusa when the situation was a little bit calmer you decided to take a day off and join your family in Ohrid on Sunday, the 12th?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say it was late in the evening on the 11th but it was early in the morning on the 12th, because I stayed there until after midnight. I don't know exactly the hour, and that's correct. In the morning, I started to Skopje because I thought that the cease-fire would enter into force which was signed on July the 5th. We signed that statement for a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when you returned from Radusa, then, on Sunday morning, you decided to go to Ohrid for one day of -- off?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My intention was to go in the morning and to return in the evening, and this was the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe now it's a good time to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So before the break, you just confirmed that on the 12th, in the morning, you started towards Ohrid. And is it correct that somewhere near Ohrid received a phone call from the deputy president of the government of Republic of Macedonia, Kemal Musliu?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the vice-president, Mr. Musliu called me on the phone. I was between Bitola and Ohrid. I don't remember the exact location where I was. I know that it was early in the morning, around 9.00, 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Vice-president Musliu is of Albanian ethnicity, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And at that time there were five Albanian ministers in the government.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the independence onwards there have always been four, five or six. I don't want to make any mistake, ministers, approximately the same number of deputies, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the deputy minister for the interior, Refet Elmazi is also of Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is an Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And during the crisis, none of his Albanians resigned from the government and the deputy minister for the interior did not leave the ministry. Is it so?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was often very present in the collegium with the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Vice-president Musliu informed you that something was happening around Ljuboten and requested some information from you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think he was as surprised as I was when he learned that something was taking place in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You tried to phone the director Goran Mitevski, but he was not available initially.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He and the others. It was Sunday earlier in the morning. I thought that they were resting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But later when you got him on the phone, you learned that he was in Ohrid as well. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure where he phoned me from. He said, We agreed that we would inform the minister together. But where he had been at the exact moment, I can't really remember. Maybe he told me, but I did not remember it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You tried to reach the minister and initially you couldn't, and then you phoned your deputy in Skopje, Mr. Ljupco Bliznakovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A correction, Ljupco Bliznakovski was not my direct deputy. He was deputy to the assistant of the minister responsible for the city of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. It was my mistake. So deputy assistant to the minister in charge of the city of Skopje so he was your direct subordinate with regard to the city of Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You actually woke him up because he returned home late the previous evening from Radusa. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was with me in Radusa.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And he was absolutely surprised by your question because he had no information that something was taking place in Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the end, through the duty operational centre you managed to speak with the Minister Boskoski. It was around 10.00 in the morning. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the first moments when you spoke with him, it did seem to you that he had just woken up. But you learned in the collegium the following morning that you found him at his barber's, actually?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I thought that he had just woken up because he was speaking very quietly and this is how I gathered this impression.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the minister was surprised by your question what was taking place in Ljuboten, because it was obvious that he knew nothing about it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. He had no information that something was taking place there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And he then told to you go to Ljuboten immediately. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you explained to him that you were near Ohrid and that you could not do it. Is that correct also?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I clarified the position where I was, the location where I was at the moment, and that I was not able to go to Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you testified, answering my learned colleague Prosecutor's question, although you started to take a vacation that day, you were in constant contact with Bliznakovski and with other, director Mitevski in order to learn what was actually taking place in Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you learned in the afternoon that hundreds of villagers of Ljuboten were walking towards Skopje and that several thousand citizens from the neighbouring villages and Skopje were walking towards Radishani and that there had already been rather chaotic, that the citizens started turning cars over, that it was already known that there were injured among the villagers leaving the village, you then, as you testified, tried, in consultation with Bliznakovski, with Mitevski, and also in consultations with the minister, decided to send to that site the posebna unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as far as you know, one part of posebna was then deployed towards Radishani and Butel in order to create a tampon zone between the thousands of citizens and villagers from Ljuboten and in order to protect the police stations that these citizens do not enter the police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you believe that through these efforts the police managed to prevent unforeseeable consequences that could have occurred on that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe we did not arrive in time to completely prevent contacts between the civilian populations. They had already occurred to the extent that they did occurred but we prevented an incident of unforeseeable consequences that we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you already had an information that some of the villagers from Ljuboten were injured in that clash with the crowd and that some of these -- or one of these people was offered medical care in a hospital?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is precisely why we have sent the posebna unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that it was only in the evening that you saw on TV that the minister had been in Ljubanci sometime later, after your phone conversation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I learned. My feedback was that it was fortunate that the minister went there so the situation calmed at the site.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that the next morning at the collegium meeting where the situation was reviewed in relation to the events of Ljuboten, the minister told you that, Goran, Bosko, you were not in Skopje and that the president told him to go on the site and try to calm the situation down. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This topic was discussed, but I could not give you precise details. But that was the spirit of the discussion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So from this testimony and from your experiences of that day, could you agree with me that neither you nor the Director Mitevski nor your direct subordinate, Ljupco Bliznakovski, and neither the minister had any information about anything that was about to take place in Ljuboten or that anyone was preparing any action?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if the police was in preparation for anything, you, of course, as the leader of the police, would naturally have that information a lot earlier. Isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And at no time the minister would skip you over or interrupt the line of hierarchy in command to suggest something to someone else or order something someone, outside of the command that would have been yours effectively. He never interfered with that line of coordination and subordination in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters kindly ask the speakers to make pauses between respective questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you answered yesterday one of the questions --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpreters asked us to make pauses.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you testified yesterday that on August 11 the minister arrived to Radusa and you stated that you were grateful for the support that he rendered to you, and in relation to the question I'm asking you now, I would like to have it repeated one more time. Is it correct that the minister didn't have any operational competences over the police officers participating in an action and he never issued such orders or he would skip over the lines of command in order to issue any such order. Is that your experience of 2001?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct, General, that immediately the next morning, when you met in the collegium, the minister informed you that he will immediately request a meeting with the representatives of the OSCE in order to ask for assistance in the activities of reviewing the Ljuboten events?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that we were given specific tasks, who should contact whom among the representatives of the international community. I know that I had soon afterwards a meeting with the NATO general in Skopje, aiming towards creating conditions for to us go on site and to make an inspection about the -- investigation about the events of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I understood you well, when you answered Prosecutor's question, you requested assistance from the NATO general. Was that General Lange [phoen] or ...

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Lange, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And General Lange told you that they could not give you support, because that was the day of the signing of the framework agreement and entry into the village could cause different problems. So is that approximately the answer you were given?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- not approximately. I remember the answer precisely. That the security assessment was -- that it was not advisable to enter the village because we would cause an even greater problem for -- from the one that had already occurred in -- if anything had occurred already.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the minister had a meeting with the head of the OSCE mission, Carlo Ungaro, since there was an information in the public domain that allegedly some people were killed in the village, and that information allegedly came from the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not only with the gentleman you mentioned. I think that the minister contacted with several ambassadors, relevant ambassadors at that time. Or political representatives in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And maybe I could refresh your memory. After those meetings, Minister Boskoski and Carlo Ungaro as well gave statements where the head of the mission stated that this was not an information released by the OSCE and that the OSCE supports the investigation of the situation, and the Minister Boskoski also immediately stated publicly that everything that took place in Ljuboten must be investigated. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And on that date, he brought a decision to establish the committee, the decision that you were shown a while ago. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as members of the commission you were immediately given the information that the investigation team established by the investigating judge Ognen Stavrev could not enter the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think they went into the entrance into the village and then they came back.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also requested assistance from the vice-president Kemal Musliu requesting that the investigation team is allowed entry into the village?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct, because I had saved the mobile phone number from which he called me on Sunday, and as he asked me, pleading that the activities there cease, I also asked him to help, if he knows some people of authority in the village, I don't know, a hodza or a priest or a teacher or something, that they could facilitate the inspection, but he briefly and categorically stated, I apologise, General, I'm sorry, but I can't help you there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that you learned that the bodies were buried and the investigation committee was prevented from entering the village for the second time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you stated that you were very frustrated by the fact, because without an on-site investigation it was practically impossible to ascertain the status of the alleged victims in the village, their number or circumstances in which these people died. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I have this feeling even now, at this moment, in a state with its constitution and laws, the police and the investigating team, investigating judge are prevented to make an inspection regarding an event in a village, in the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that you stated this now, is it true, General, that actually, pursuant to the Law on Criminal Procedure of the Republic of Macedonia when there is a well-based suspicion that a crime has been committed, then it is normal and the only possible situation is that the police, through its duty operational centre, informs the duty public prosecutor and the duty investigating judge and then the judge on duty decides who will perform the on-site investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Pursuant to the Law on Criminal Procedure, the on-site investigation is carried out by the investigating judge in the presence of a public prosecutor; if he concludes, based on the information received, that the case is insignificant in terms of consequences, the damage caused, etc., he can refer the on-site investigation to a team from the Ministry of the Interior. Which usually happens in case of minor traffic accidents, just to clarify…

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also answered my next question, if these are minor incidents, then the investigating judge authorises the police to conduct the on-site investigation on their own. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But once the judge decides to go on the scene, he decides what will be the team to accompany him, so he calls for an establishment of a team of forensics -- criminal forensics, and other police team that will secure the site or assist the court if it deems it necessary, it calls forensic pathologists or other persons that are important to establish the facts, experts from various fields and then it is the judge who decides about all the actions taken on the scene. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The judge who makes the on-site investigation is the dominus litis of this entire activity and all the others are only acting upon his order. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I don't speak English, if dominus litis means head or chief, then this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As I said --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, "I don't understand Latin" was what he precisely said.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And in Latin it means exactly what you said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Tell me now -- could we look -- I was warned that there might be a mistake somewhere. Line 23, my question was -- page 73, line 23, my question was: So that during minor incidents that are less important, that investigating judge may authorise the police to carry out the on-site investigation itself. That is in line -- in line 23 has been said that the police decides by itself, which was not my question. Thank you. General, could you look at the document in tab 117. That is Exhibit 1D6. Let's immediately see the second page, which is N000-7351. The English bears the same number with addition of the ET. Do you see this document, Official Note of the Basic Court II and the second document that I said -- that I asked you to review is the -- signed by the investigating judge Ognen Stavrev.

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that page, it is said: "Regarding the same case on the 12th of August, the duty investigating judge was informed by MVR SVR DOC 92 at 1730 that in the area of the Ljubanci and Ljuboten villages, there were several murdered members of the paramilitaries of the Albanian terrorists, but no one could come close to the bodies because at that moment the military activities were still going on. "The investigative judge informed the deputy public prosecutor, Roska Karova about the details that he received by the MVR. The investigating judge was also informed that the safety of the investigation authorities of the court and the public prosecution was not guaranteed because of the clashes that were still going on. So that is why no investigation activities were undertaken, more precisely because of the military clashes that were still ongoing between the mentioned paramilitary formations and the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia. "Dr. Aleksej Duma was also informed about it, this director of the Forensic Institute and criminology." General, is it obvious from this report that the competent bodies of the police, through the duty operational centre of the city of Skopje, already on the 12th, in the late afternoon hours, informed the judge that it is possible that there might be deceased persons in the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the police has acted upon its duties and obligations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So by informing the investigating judge the police completed its legal obligation. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The police provided additional information about the situation but is it correct, General, that the investigating judge is the one to-- to decide whether they're going to carry out the investigation regardless of the security situation on the village whether they would enter into combat activities or into some situation that is not very certain that is a decision of the investigating judge himself and only the investigating judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you look now at the first page of the document. That is N000-7350. And this is an Official Note, speaking of two attempts of the investigating judge Ognen Stavrev, the deputy Milan Gelevski and Zlatko Jakovski from the forensics and criminalistics pathology institute to carry out a on-site investigation. Tell me, is that the time when you made efforts through NATO through the vice-president of the government and through some other international entities to help the investigating team enter the village?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the entire leadership was standing on their feet trying to provide conditions for the investigating judge and the prosecutor and the others of the investigation team to be able access the village. Unfortunately, that didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of this commission established by the minister, which is in tab 96, as the first document of this binder, and that is Exhibit P73, you -- you already were handicapped by the fact that you were not able to determine the first and the primary facts that are important for any type of procedure that might be taken by the police in relation to these events. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But at the question of my learned colleague the Prosecutor you said that in line with the order given in the decision, you tried to get all the available materials from the services of the Ministry of Interior, so you would be able to come to an information what had really been going on there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that the biggest part of that work was done by the president of the commission. That is Goran Mitevski, right?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And knowing him as an exceptional professional you had total faith in his work and that he would do anything to learn about the circumstances and that he would find all the relevant documents that are necessary. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that since it was -- the uniformed police was your competence, through your line, through your deputy -- not your deputy but the deputy of the assistant minister for Skopje, Ljupco Bliznakovski, you have tried to find out what had really happened and what the situation were in the police stations on the field. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. I would just like to add not only with Ljupco but the entire team of mine with the people that were composing the leadership of the police departments with my immediate collaborators had the task to gather information about the Ljuboten events.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you had absolute trust in Ljupco Bliznakovski as a professional, as an exceptional police professional?

utterances.speaker: RISTO GALEVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my learned colleague the Prosecutor asked me to -- to -- to stop my cross-examination some five minutes before the end of the session because he has a question, so I don't know whether this is right time now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think this is the appropriate time. Thank you for that, Ms. Residovic. We must continue tomorrow with the evidence of the General at 9.00. You will appreciate that, General, and in view of that, the court officer will now be able to show you out of the court and we'll deal with whatever this further matter may be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber has just explored with counsel the question of whether the planned witness to follow the present witness will be able to conclude his evidence before the commencement of the break. The time indications given by counsel indicate that that will not be feasible and in those circumstances, the Chamber indicates that it would in its view, not be in the interests of justice to have a significant break in the course of the evidence of that witness, and that therefore the alternative course proposed by Mr. Saxon should be followed, which is that at the end of the evidence of the present witness a crime base witness who can be available should be called and that witness will proceed on the basis that the Chamber will ensure, by cutting short counsel if necessary, that the evidence of that witness concludes by the end of the session on Friday. Is that clear enough for everybody? Very well. We now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
